## Discovery & Translational Science

* **[Big Pharma]** **Moderna and Merck advance personalized neoantigen selection algorithm for mRNA cancer vaccine** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/27/moderna-merck-cancer-vaccine-secret-ingredient-an-algorithm/)
  * Analysis highlights the computational algorithm driving mRNA-4157 (V940), a personalized neoantigen therapy co-developed by Moderna and Merck.
  * The system utilizes predictive modeling to identify patient-specific tumor mutations most likely to generate robust HLA-presented neoepitopes for targeted T-cell responses.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Real-world trial links Eli Lilly's Zepbound to reduced total healthcare expenditure** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/zepbound-costs-ivonescimab-mckesson-sentivera-imaavy-bausch/828680/)
  * A real-world study published in *Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism* evaluated adults 55 years and older with obesity or overweight receiving Zepbound (tirzepatide).
  * Adherence to tirzepatide was associated with a monthly per-patient cost reduction of $181 at 6 months and $607 at 12 months compared to non-users, driven predominantly by fewer emergency room visits and hospitalizations.

* **Trigeminal nerve stimulation induces persistent hippocampal plasticity across species** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.25.26361320)
  * Intermittent 200 Hz trigeminal nerve stimulation (i200-TNS) elicited sustained CA1 field excitatory postsynaptic potential potentiation and prolonged neuronal firing in rodent models, dependent on locus coeruleus activity.
  * In human stereo-EEG monitoring, i200-TNS increased hippocampal theta-gamma coupling and improved delayed recall performance in a randomized crossover study.

* **PLACO genomic analysis reveals divergent liver-fat pathway in CAD and T2D genetic risk** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.24.26361276)
  * A multi-ancestry pleiotropy analysis identified 149 shared genomic loci between type 2 diabetes (T2D) and coronary artery disease (CAD), with 35 of 42 novel loci demonstrating discordant directionality.
  * Mendelian randomization and biomarker clustering showed that liver fat accumulation represents a distinct mechanistic axis driving divergent disease risks.

* **Preclinical bispecific CZ105 Bis2 suppresses disease activity in SLE models** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42657656/)
  * Researchers evaluated CZ105 Bis2, a bispecific antibody targeting B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and interleukin-21 (IL-21), in models of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).
  * Dual inhibition reduced pathogenic autoantibody titers and attenuated end-organ renal damage compared to single-pathway controls.

* **Ncbe identified as primary basolateral Na⁺ transport mechanism in choroid plexus** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.24.745951)
  * Fluorometric Na⁺ imaging using Sodium Binding Fluorescent Indicator demonstrated that the Na⁺-dependent Cl⁻/HCO₃⁻ exchanger Ncbe (*Slc4a10*) regulates intracellular Na⁺ loading in choroid plexus epithelial cells.
  * Extracellular Na⁺ depletion reduced ex vivo intracellular [Na⁺] from ~54 mM to ~5 mM in the presence of CO₂/HCO₃⁻, defining its role in cerebrospinal fluid secretion.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **Spyre Therapeutics halts SPY072 monotherapy development in rheumatoid arthritis** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/spyre-rheumatoid-arthritis-drug-study-results-skyway/828809/)
  * SPY072, an anti-TL1A monoclonal antibody, met study objectives and demonstrated proof-of-mechanism in a Phase 2 trial for rheumatoid arthritis, but failed to meet internal efficacy thresholds for monotherapy.
  * Spyre will discontinue development in RA to focus on ongoing Phase 2 evaluations in psoriatic arthritis and axial spondyloarthritis, with readouts scheduled for Q4.

* **Phase 2 basket trial demonstrates activity of T-DM1 in HER2-amplified solid tumors** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42658187/)
  * A Phase 2 basket trial evaluated ado-trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) across multiple non-breast, non-gastric HER2-amplified advanced solid malignancies.
  * The trial established proof-of-concept efficacy and manageable safety in heavily pretreated patient cohorts harboring confirmed *ERBB2* amplifications.

* **Azacitidine plus ruxolitinib Phase 2 combination trial completes in myelofibrosis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.org/42657929/)
  * Final results of a Phase 2 trial combining the hypomethylating agent azacitidine with the JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor ruxolitinib in myelofibrosis patients evaluated spleen volume response and symptom control.
  * The regimen demonstrated manageable hematologic toxicity and sustained clinical improvement in patients with sub-optimal response to ruxolitinib monotherapy.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **AstraZeneca and Amgen’s Tezspire achieves Phase 3 success in eosinophilic esophagitis** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/astrazeneca-amgen-tezpire-eosinophilic-esophagitis-results/828946/)
  * Tezspire (tezepelumab), an anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody, met all co-primary and secondary endpoints in a Phase 3 study for patients with eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE).
  * Treatment achieved statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in histological disease activity and clinical symptoms at 24 weeks, with efficacy sustained through 52 weeks.

* **[Biotech]** **Verrica Pharmaceuticals completes enrollment in pivotal Phase 3 COVE-2 trial for YCANTH** [X / BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2092945987610304584)
  * Verrica completed patient enrollment in its Phase 3 COVE-2 trial evaluating YCANTH (cantharidin 0.7% topical solution) for the treatment of common warts.
  * Topline efficacy and safety data from the pivotal registration trial are anticipated in Q1 2027.

* **[Biotech]** **Invivyd nears readout for Phase 3/3b DECLARATION trial of COVID-19 mAb** [X / BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2092783335189762507)
  * Invivyd is entering the final weeks of patient data collection for its DECLARATION study evaluating its monoclonal antibody platform for COVID-19 pre-exposure prophylaxis.
  * Data collection coincides with rising regional infection rates across active clinical study sites.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Biotech]** **FDA grants priority approval to Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque for advanced pancreatic cancer** [FDA Press Release](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-class-targeted-therapy-metastatic-pancreatic-cancer)
  * The FDA approved Rasonque (daraxonrasib), a first-in-class daily oral RAS GTPase inhibitor, for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma following prior systemic therapy or who are ineligible for multiagent regimens.
  * Approval was supported by the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial (NCT06625320), where daraxonrasib significantly improved overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) compared to physician's choice chemotherapy.
  * Revolution Medicines set the list price at $39,800 per 30-day supply (~$477,000 annually).

* **[Biotech]** **CytomX Therapeutics receives FDA Fast Track Designation for varsetatug masetecan in colorectal cancer** [X / BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2092945562802798951)
  * The FDA granted Fast Track Designation to varsetatug masetecan for the treatment of patients with relapsed/refractory metastatic colorectal cancer (R/R mCRC).

* **FDA warns against dietary supplement-grade glutathione following 30 intravenous adverse events** [FDA Alert](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/human-drug-compounding/fda-reminds-compounders-not-use-dietary-supplement-grade-glutathione-injectables)
  * The FDA alerted healthcare providers to at least 30 cases of severe adverse events—including fever, chills, dizziness, and sepsis-like symptoms—linked to IV glutathione compounded from dietary supplement-grade material (Lot #229536, distributed by Medisca Inc.).
  * Two Texas compounding facilities initiated voluntary recalls due to elevated endotoxin levels, which pose severe systemic safety risks.

* **Baxter initiates voluntary recall of saline and citrate solutions over glass particulate contamination** [FDA Recalls](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/baxter-issues-voluntary-nationwide-recall-two-lots-09-sodium-chloride-injection-due-potential)
  * Baxter International voluntarily recalled two lots of 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection (500 mL) and one lot of Anticoagulant Sodium Citrate Solution (250 mL) due to particulate matter identified as fiberglass.
  * Intravenous administration of glass particulates carries risks of microvascular embolization, phlebitis, organ inflammation, and pulmonary tissue damage.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Biotech]** **Biohaven licenses Kv7 ion channel candidate opakalim to SK Biopharmaceuticals in $795M agreement** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biohaven-sk-opakalim-epilepsy-drug-deal/828799/)
  * Biohaven partnered with SK Biopharmaceuticals to transfer global rights for its Kv7 ion channel platform, including Phase 3 focal epilepsy candidate opakalim.
  * Biohaven receives $350M up front, $50M in 2027, and up to $150M in regulatory/development milestones, plus royalties, while SK assumes up to $245M in obligations to Knopp Biosciences. Topline Phase 3 Rise3 trial data are expected by year-end.

* **[Biotech]** **Insitro highlights machine-learning framework to accelerate clinical trial execution** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/26/biotech-insitro-ceo-daphne-koller-speeding-up-clinical-trials-ai-prognosis/)
  * Insitro CEO Daphne Koller outlined the biotech's strategy to utilize artificial intelligence platforms for patient stratification, prognostic modeling, and biomarker identification to optimize clinical trial execution and timelines.

* **[Biotech]** **Outer Bio exits stealth with long-term ex vivo human skin culture platform** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/outer-bio-skin-biotech-michael-polansky-cosmetics-pharma/828910/)
  * Startup Outer Bio launched with a platform that maintains living human skin tissue samples ex vivo for up to one month, retaining tissue architecture and resident immune cells.
  * Led by CEO Michael Polansky, the company integrates high-throughput tissue profiling with AI screening to discover targets for dermatologic conditions and skincare formulations.

## Public Health & Policy

* **FDA extends DSCSA compliance exemptions for small dispensers to late 2027** [FDA Guidance](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-supply-chain-security-act-dscsa/exemptions-under-drug-supply-chain-security-act)
  * The FDA announced an extension of Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) Section 582 compliance exemptions for small dispensers (pharmacies with ≤25 licensed pharmacists or technicians) until November 27, 2027.
  * The extension provides additional time for small dispensers to complete baseline security assessments and transition toward full electronic interoperable drug distribution tracking.

* **FDA outlines CNPV pilot program to expedite reviews for critical national health priorities** [FDA Announcement](http://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)
  * The FDA released details on the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program, aimed at accelerating NDA/BLA review times using a collaborative review model.
  * The program targets candidates aligned with five national priorities: public health crisis response, emerging biological threats, innovative breakthrough therapies, high unmet medical need, and supply chain/onshoring resilience.

* **U.S. health systems prepare lobbying strategy against proposed $1T Medicaid spending cuts** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/27/hospitals-lobby-reverse-medicaid-cuts-part-2-unraveled-series/)
  * Hospital trade groups and healthcare systems are organizing legislative opposition to anticipated federal cuts totaling $1 trillion in Medicaid funding.
  * Industry leaders warn that proposed reductions threaten safety-net hospitals, uncompensated care reimbursement, and clinical service availability.

**Worth watching:** Revolution Medicines' commercial rollout of Rasonque will be an essential benchmark for pricing power and adoption rates of pan-RAS targeted therapies in gastrointestinal oncology.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Pancreatic Cancer Risk is High - Why?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gr8mi7dvE5A) -- Physionic
        - Hyperinsulinemia acts via acinar insulin receptors to initiate pancreatic cancer development by promoting inflammation and digestive enzyme production.
        - Elevated insulin concentrations stimulate pancreatic cancer cell proliferation and glucose uptake by activating MAP kinase and PI3 kinase signaling pathways while upregulating GLUT-1 expression.
        - High extracellular glucose levels accelerate cancer cell growth through EGF expression and EGFR transactivation, drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition via hydrogen peroxide production, and induce perineural invasion.
        - Population cohort studies demonstrate a direct incremental risk between elevated fasting glucose levels, diabetes, and the development of pancreatic cancer and pancreatic cystic neoplasms.
    - [‘Off Target’ Effects of GLP1 Peptides](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/zW9RJ89FWS8) -- Physionic
        - GLP-1 receptor agonists demonstrate off-target benefits beyond fat loss, including improved liver health markers and potential attenuation or partial reversal of osteoarthritis-related structural changes.
        - Preclinical evaluations of retatrutide show sustained energy expenditure despite weight loss, contrasting with the metabolic rate reduction typically induced by caloric restriction.
        - The energy expenditure-preserving effects observed with retatrutide remain unverified in human clinical trials, leaving the finding preliminary.
        - Gastrointestinal side effects remain a primary limitation of GLP-1 peptide therapies, requiring clinical monitoring during treatment.
    - [Why Product-Led Growth Doesn’t Work in Healthcare](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/AnDMaK0irGc) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Dr. Simon Los addresses the requirement to decouple back-end system architecture from front-end end-user experiences in medical software.
        - Standard consumer-market product-led growth (PLG) strategies fail to translate effectively into healthcare environments due to structural industry differences.
        - Sustainable digital health adoption requires deployment strategies designed specifically for clinical workflows rather than self-serve consumer acquisition models.
    - [The AI Scribe Gold Rush Is Already Over](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Bz-KFALQ1kY) -- Digital Health Inside Out
        - Dr. Simon Kos asserts that foundational speech-to-text transcription and basic clinical note generation are no longer sufficient competitive differentiators for AI scribes.
        - The initial wave of market entry for simple medical transcription tools has plateaued as basic note generation becomes commoditized.
        - Next-generation healthcare AI products must offer advanced clinical functionality beyond automated documentation to maintain market viability.
- Pure Science
    - [We Took $10,000 From @mkbhd's Locked iPhone](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/b3KpFdb1pW8) -- Veritasium
        - A vulnerability within specific virtual wallet software architectures enables unauthorized financial transactions from secured mobile devices.
        - Researchers demonstrated the security flaw by extracting $10,000 from a locked iPhone belonging to tech reviewer Marques Brownlee (@mkbhd).
        - The demonstration highlights underlying authentication and transaction processing flaws present in select contactless payment implementations.
